overview: This one-page State Department list-of-papers sheet records a 1940 matter concerning Mitsui and Company Limited’s desire to secure the services of the J. G. White Engineering Corporation to plan and construct hydraulic and steam power plants in Japan. It refers to a conversation with Gano Dunn, the engineering corporation’s president, and appears to have been routed to the Department’s Far Eastern Affairs office through Mackay.

subfiles.title: List-of-papers entry on Mitsui’s proposed power-plant engineering contract
subfiles.about: The sheet records Mitsui and Company Limited’s interest in hiring the J. G. White Engineering Corporation to plan and erect hydraulic and steam power plants in Japan.
subfiles.summary: This filing sheet describes a conversation with Gano Dunn, president of the J. G. White Engineering Corporation. The subject was Mitsui and Company Limited’s desire to obtain the corporation’s services for planning and constructing hydraulic and steam power plants in Japan. The sheet was associated with the State Department’s Far Eastern Affairs office and bears a November 25, 1940 entry.

interest: Although only a filing summary, this document identifies a specific instance of proposed Japanese procurement of American engineering expertise in 1940. It is useful for tracing Mitsui’s infrastructure ambitions, U.S.–Japanese commercial and technical relations immediately before the Pacific War, and the State Department’s monitoring of industrial projects with potential strategic significance.
